# Design Document ## Overview Three parts: 1. **Geometry** (`geometry/booleans.py`): one function `combine_parts(parts)` that folds an ordered list of `(outline, mode)` parts with pathops, a `divide(outlines)` that returns pieces tagged with their top-most source, and `split_regions(segments)` that breaks a result into connected areas (each with its holes). skia-pathops already provides every operation needed (`UNION`, `DIFFERENCE`, `INTERSECTION`, `XOR`), per-contour orientation, `area` and `contains`. 2. **Operations** (`editing/operations/booleans.py`, new): `combine(session, op)` for union / difference / intersection / exclude, and `divide_selection(session)`. They move out of `paths.py`, which keeps Object to Path only. Five registered commands. 3. **Views** (`views/keymap.py`, icons): bindings, Path menu and tool strip entries, three new Tabler icons. No model changes: every result is a plain `PathShape`. ## Steering Document Alignment ### Technical Standards (tech.md) - Pure, Qt-free geometry in `geometry/`; state changes only in operations through `session.edit(label)`; presentation only in `views/keymap.py`. The architecture test keeps holding. - skia-pathops stays the boolean engine (float32 inside; results rounded by the existing `_from_skia`). ### Project Structure (structure.md) - New module `editing/operations/booleans.py`, one concern per module: `paths.py` shrinks to Object to Path. - Tests: `tests/geometry/test_booleans.py` (extended) and `tests/editing/test_booleans.py` (combine and divide moved from `test_paths.py`, plus new cases). ## Code Reuse Analysis ### Existing Components to Leverage - **`geometry.booleans._to_skia / _from_skia`**: segment ↔ pathops conversion, unchanged. - **`geometry.transforms.outline`**: transformed outlines of rect/ellipse/path (text stays `None`, so it's excluded as today). - **`editing.queries.can_combine`**: "two or more shapes with an outline" check for all five commands. - **`operations._document.new_id`**: ids for results and pieces. - **Existing `combine` z-order logic**: the result replaces the bottom-most selected shape in its layer; generalized to "insert a list of shapes there" so divide can reuse it. ### Integration Points - **Registry**: `path.union`, `path.difference` keep their ids; new `path.intersection`, `path.exclude`, `path.divide`. - **Keymap**: Path menu `[union, difference, intersection, exclude, divide, None, object_to_path]`; tool strip gets all five after the tools. - **Icons**: `scripts/generate_icons.py` mapping + `icons.py` constants `INTERSECTION`, `EXCLUDE`, `DIVIDE`. ## Architecture ```mermaid graph TD K[views/keymap.py
shortcuts, icons, layouts] --> A[views/actions.py] A --> R[editing/registry.py] R --> OB[editing/operations/booleans.py
combine, divide_selection] OB --> GB[geometry/booleans.py
combine_parts, divide, split_regions] OB --> T[geometry/transforms.outline] GB --> PO[skia-pathops] ``` ## Components and Interfaces ### `geometry/booleans.py` ```python Mode = Literal["add", "subtract", "intersect", "exclude"] _PATHOPS = {"add": UNION, "subtract": DIFFERENCE, "intersect": INTERSECTION, "exclude": XOR} def combine_parts(parts: Sequence[tuple[Segments, Mode]]) -> Segments: """Starts from the first part's outline (whatever its mode) and applies each following part with its mode.""" def divide(outlines: Sequence[Segments]) -> list[tuple[Segments, int]]: """Every area covered by a different set of outlines, split into connected regions. Each piece is tagged with the index of the top-most outline covering it.""" def split_regions(segments: Segments) -> list[Segments]: """Connected areas of a simplified outline, each with the holes inside it.""" ``` **`combine_parts`**: converts each outline once, folds with `pathops.op(result, part, _PATHOPS[mode])`, converts back once at the end. An empty list or an empty result returns `()`. **`divide`** (incremental, roughly quadratic in the number of outlines instead of exponential over subsets): ``` pieces = [] # (pathops.Path, top_index) for index, outline in enumerate(outlines): shape = to_skia(outline) covered = union of all earlier outlines (kept incrementally) next_pieces = [] for piece, top in pieces: inside = piece ∩ shape -> (inside, index) # now covered by this outline too outside = piece − shape -> (outside, top) keep both if not empty remainder = shape − covered -> (remainder, index) pieces = next_pieces (+ remainder) then each piece -> split_regions -> drop regions with area < MIN_PIECE_AREA ``` **`split_regions`**: simplifies, then for every contour counts how many other contours contain its first point (`contour.contains`). An even count means an outer boundary, an odd count means a hole. Each hole is attached to the smallest-area outer contour that contains it at depth − 1. Islands inside holes come out as their own regions. Pure pathops, no skia-python. **`MIN_PIECE_AREA`** = 1e-3 square document units: float32 slivers along shared edges stay below it, while real shapes even at extreme zoom don't. `boolean(outlines, op)` (today's API) is replaced. Its callers move to `combine_parts`, so destructive booleans and the future Composite share one code path (Requirement 5.3). ### `editing/operations/booleans.py` ```python OPERATIONS = {"union": ("add", "Union"), "difference": ("subtract", "Difference"), "intersection": ("intersect", "Intersection"), "exclude": ("exclude", "Exclude")} def combine(session, op: str) -> None def divide_selection(session) -> None ``` - **`combine`** collects the selected shapes that have an outline (bottom to top). Inside `session.edit(name)` it computes `combine_parts([(outline, mode) for each])`. A non-empty result becomes a new `PathShape` with the bottom shape's style; an empty one leaves nothing and sets the status to "{name} is empty". The new shapes are inserted with `_replace_with(state, targets, new_shapes)`. - **`divide_selection`** works the same way through `geometry.booleans.divide`. Each piece becomes a `PathShape` styled like `targets[top_index]`. Pieces are sorted by `top_index` (stable), so pieces from higher shapes stay above lower ones. All pieces end up selected, and the status reads "Divided into N pieces". - **`_replace_with(state, targets, new_shapes)`**: removes the consumed shapes and inserts `new_shapes` in order at the bottom-most target's position in its layer. This generalizes today's combine loop. - Registration: `path.union` "&Union", `path.difference` "D&ifference", `path.intersection` "&Intersection", `path.exclude` "E&xclude", `path.divide` "Di&vide". All use `can_combine` as their check. ### `views/keymap.py` and icons | id | label | shortcut | icon (Tabler) | |---|---|---|---| | `path.union` | &Union | Ctrl++ | layers-union (existing) | | `path.difference` | D&ifference | Ctrl+- | layers-subtract (existing) | | `path.intersection` | &Intersection | Ctrl+* | `layers-intersect-2` (hatched overlap) | | `path.exclude` | E&xclude | Ctrl+^ | `layers-difference` (overlap dashed out) | | `path.divide` | Di&vide | Ctrl+/ | `layers-intersect` (all edges drawn) | **Keyboard caveat:** on layouts where `^` is a dead key (German, French, …), Ctrl+^ may never reach Qt as a shortcut. I'll verify it on your keyboard during implementation. If it doesn't fire, Exclude gets a second binding (Ctrl+Alt+X), while Ctrl+^ stays for Inkscape familiarity on other layouts. ## Data Models No changes. Results are `PathShape(id, segments, style)` with identity transform. ## Error Handling ### Error Scenarios 1. **Empty result** (intersection without overlap, exclude of identical shapes, difference that cuts everything). - **Handling:** the consumed shapes are removed and nothing is created. The status reads "{Operation} is empty". It's one undo step, so Ctrl+Z restores everything. - **User Impact:** the shapes disappear with a clear message and can be undone. 2. **pathops failure** (`PathOpsError` on degenerate input such as zero-area outlines). - **Handling:** caught in the operation *before* `session.edit` mutates anything (geometry runs first, then the edit applies the result). The status reads "{Operation} failed". - **User Impact:** nothing changes, and there's no crash. 3. **Slivers from float32 rounding in divide.** - **Handling:** pieces under `MIN_PIECE_AREA` are dropped. ## Testing Strategy ### Unit Testing - **`tests/geometry/test_booleans.py`**: - `combine_parts`: each mode on overlapping squares (area and bbox); a first part with a non-add mode; non-overlapping intersect returns `()`; exclude of three overlapping squares (triple overlap filled again); results identical to the old union/difference tests. - `split_regions`: two disjoint squares give 2 regions; a square with a hole gives 1 region with 2 contours; an island inside a hole gives 2 regions. - `divide`: two overlapping squares give 3 pieces with the right top indices; a ring cut by a bar gives disconnected pieces split; identical squares give 1 piece; sliver filtering. - **`tests/editing/test_booleans.py`**: the union/difference tests moved from `test_paths.py`, plus intersection (empty and non-empty, style and z-order from the bottom shape), exclude, divide (piece count, styles from the top-most source, selection, z-order, one undo step and undo restores ids/order), disabled with fewer than two outlines or text-only selections, and undo labels. - **`tests/views/test_keymap.py`**: unchanged test, now also covering the new ids. ### Integration Testing - A QTest scratch script: select overlapping shapes, trigger each command via its shortcut (including the dead-key check for Ctrl+^ on your layout) and via the tool strip. Run offscreen and on desktop GL. ### End-to-End Testing - The screenshot shows the extended tool strip and Path menu. A visual check of a divided rect+ellipse.
